lineas.texto: Ever wondered how an eraser actually removes pencil?
A pencil has no lead. It's graphite, stacked layers of carbon that slide off like a deck of cards.
When you write, tiny flakes break off and land on the paper fibers.
They never soak in. They just sit on top, held by friction.
Now here comes the eraser. Its rubber is a little sticky, stickier than the paper.
As you rub, it grabs the flakes and pulls them right off the fibers.
The rubber wears away too, rolling the graphite into those little crumbs.
Pen ink is different. It soaks deep into the fibers, so the eraser can't reach it.
